title: Blackwell, Oklahoma · May 25, 1955
summary: Compare historical accounts, reported clock conventions and aftermath. The Blackwell and Udall tornadoes remain separate, and the surviving accounts do not establish a continuous visual reconstruction.

records.basis: Reviewed association: the May 25, 1955 Kay County F5 record at 21:26 CST with 20 direct deaths matches the NWS Norman Blackwell table. County segment length remains 19.6 miles; it is not replaced by the whole-track length. The NWS narrative and table use different time labels, so the original NCEI clock is retained.

observations.title: How Norman's historical listing was reviewed
observations.locator: Sections 2 and 3, printed pages 1 to 2 (PDF pages 3 to 4). Section 4C, printed pages 4 to 5 (PDF pages 6 to 7). Section 4D and conclusion, printed pages 6 to 7 (PDF pages 8 to 9).
observations.account: Speheger describes a review of 1950 to 1995 tornado records for the Norman forecast area. Earlier records were compared with climatological publications, and later records with Storm Data. The web listing replaced coordinate tracks with descriptions relative to towns. Changes required a clear error or sufficient supporting evidence. Unresolved discrepancies were retained. The report also distinguishes a storm's path from individual tornadoes within a family.
observations.limits: This is the methodology behind the listing linked by NWS Norman, not a new Blackwell survey. The inspected passages do not reconcile Blackwell's clock labels, injury counts or differing path lengths. No county rows are merged, and no new track or coordinates are registered.

media.title: A severe-thunderstorm bulletin that names Blackwell
media.locator: NWS Wichita archive, First Warning Issued link; complete surviving 609 by 409 pixel image. The line naming Blackwell to Winfield and eastward is separate from the earlier Kansas and Missouri paragraph with a noon ending.
media.account: The document reports morning thunderstorms and rain amounts, explicitly adds Blackwell to Winfield and areas eastward to a severe-thunderstorm area, and reports an Arkansas River observation at 11.15 AM. The archive supplies May 25, 1955 event context. The opening Kansas and Missouri paragraph has a period ending at noon.
media.limits: The crop does not identify an issue date, issuing office or time zone. Morning conditions do not establish exact morning issuance. The noon ending cannot be assigned to the later Blackwell-area addition. Collection context is not a printed document date. No Blackwell receipt, tornado lead time, warning polygon or synchronized event clock is established.

media.title: A broad severe-weather forecast and its later caption
media.locator: NWS Wichita archive, Second Warning Issued link; complete 608 by 436 pixel image including the typewritten forecast and later archive caption. Issue, valid-period and caption broadcast labels are kept distinct.
media.account: The typewritten forecast describes possible tornadoes across a large city-defined region and requests immediate broadcast. Its heading has May 25 and an overtyped 4.36 PM issue label; the forecast period is 4.30 PM to 10 PM. The later archive caption supplies May 25, 1955, gives 4:36 P.M. and reports a broadcast by local media on the 5:00 news.
media.limits: The year and broadcast assertion belong to the later caption, not the typewritten body. No independent station record was obtained. Neither layer identifies a time zone, Blackwell broadcaster or resident who received it. The city-defined area is not converted into a polygon or explicit Blackwell warning. No tornado lead time or absolute event clock is derived.

place.reported: A broad region described through Dodge City, Amarillo, Wichita Falls, Ardmore and Wichita. This is attributed area wording, not a plotted warning polygon or explicit Blackwell receipt.
